item.title: What is the WASDE report: Why USDA Cut Corn Stocks 91M Bushels
item.description: USDA's WASDE is a monthly checkbook for each crop, and this season's corn ending-stocks estimate shows why it keeps moving: cut in August and September, raised in October, then cut 91 million bushels in November on a smaller yield and lower exports. The twist is that the price forecast still went down while South America's crops went up.

item.title: Hedge Funds Are Short 63K Hog Contracts. Who's Left to Sell?
item.description: Hedge funds sold lean hogs for 4 straight weeks and now hold their most bearish hog bet in 3 years, and the November WASDE also expects cheaper hogs and more pork. But this week's selling was the smallest of the streak, so the crowd may be nearly out of sellers.

item.title: US Wheat Exports Drop to 750M Bushels as Russia, EU Lead
item.description: USDA's November world numbers put Russia at the top of the wheat export race with the EU, Canada and Australia close behind, while the US trails the pack. The data shows a smaller US crop and a smaller US export forecast in a world with more wheat to go around, and hedge funds are still betting on lower prices.

item.title: Hedge Funds Sold 404K Corn Contracts. Commercial Hedgers Bought 334K
item.description: This week's corn data shows why hedge funds and commercial hedgers are almost always on opposite sides: funds sold 404 thousand contracts since late September and flipped net short, while commercials' net position rose 334 thousand. Funds trade the price and commercials trade the grain, and knowing that tells a farmer who is on the other side of every bushel sold.

item.title: Funds Cut Cattle Bets to a Near 3-Year Low, Yet USDA Sees $238 Steers
item.description: Hedge funds sold live cattle for a second straight week and now hold their smallest bullish bet in almost 3 years, even though USDA, the referee, forecasts less beef and higher fed steer prices. With most of the fund crowd already out and prices firming after the snapshot, the selling looks closer to its end than its start.

item.title: Who Fills China's 115M-Ton Soybean Order: Brazil or the US?
item.description: China imports 115 million tons of soybeans while growing only 21 million, which makes it the bidder behind the soybean market. Brazil is the biggest seller, yet USDA just raised US soybean exports and cut US stocks, while hedge funds were still trimming a big bullish bet.

item.title: USDA Cut Corn Crop 141M Bushels, Then Cut Its Price Forecast Too
item.description: USDA's November WASDE cut corn yield, production and ending stocks, taking back part of October's big increase, after hedge funds had spent 7 straight weeks selling their way to a nearly flat position. Yet USDA also lowered its corn price forecast, with exports trimmed and South American crops raised.

item.title: Corn Funds Sold 7 Weeks Straight. How to Read It in the COT Report
item.description: This week's corn data teaches the whole COT report: hedge funds sold for 7 straight weeks and are nearly flat, yet against the last 3 years they still rank in the 62nd percentile, a ranking analysts calculate from the report rather than one the CFTC prints. To read the report you need the level, the change, that historical context, and the commercials taking the other side.

item.title: Brazil Grows 186M Tons of Soybeans. The US Edge Is at Home
item.description: USDA's own world balance sheet shows Brazil growing and exporting far more soybeans than the US, with China as the one giant buyer both chase. The US edge is at home in the crush plant, and the news this week flags weather as Brazil's one weak spot.

item.title: Cattle Funds at 26th Percentile While Steers Head to $238
item.description: USDA sees egg prices resetting and fed steer prices climbing and holding through 2027, but hedge funds, usually quick to chase a strong trend, are only now starting to buy cattle from the bearish side of their recent range.

item.title: Funds Sold 1.67 Billion Bushels of Corn, Yet Are Still Net Long
item.description: Hedge funds sold corn hard for 6 straight weeks, about 1.67 billion bushels on paper, but corn is only one part of the crowd map: funds hold their most bearish hog position in 3 years, both wheats are now net short, soy is still a crowded long, and cattle was the only market they bought.
